blocks.md:
1. [Econ 430 L1 Univariate Characterizations](note:econ-430-l1-univariate-characterizations)
2. [Econ 430 L2 Bivariate Characterizations](note:econ-430-l2-bivariate-characterizations)
3. [Econ 430 L3 The Method of Least Squares](note:econ-430-l3-the-method-of-least-squares)
4. [Econ 430 L4 Cross-Validation and the Bootstrap](note:econ-430-l4-cross-validation-and-the-bootstrap)
5. [Econ 430 L5 Estimating Nonlinear Relationships](note:econ-430-l5-estimating-nonlinear-relationships)
6. [Econ 430 L6 Indicator Variables and the OLS Workflow](note:econ-430-l6-indicator-variables-and-the-ols-workflow)
7. [Econ 430 L7 The Classical Linear Regression Model](note:econ-430-l7-the-classical-linear-regression-model)
L1 to L7 come from one notebook, `Regression_Lecture1_Adv.ipynb`, one lecture per major heading.

The course starts by **looking at the data**. [Econ 430 L1 Univariate Characterizations](note:econ-430-l1-univariate-characterizations) describes each variable on its own, with summary statistics, [Skewness and Kurtosis](note:skewness-and-kurtosis), histograms, [Kernel Density Estimation](note:kernel-density-estimation), the [Q-Q Plot](note:q-q-plot) and the [Cullen-Frey Graph](note:cullen-frey-graph); [Econ 430 L2 Bivariate Characterizations](note:econ-430-l2-bivariate-characterizations) looks at pairs, with scatterplots and the [Lowess Smoother](note:lowess-smoother) as a first check of linearity.

[Econ 430 L3 The Method of Least Squares](note:econ-430-l3-the-method-of-least-squares) is the core. It starts from the [Simple Linear Regression Model](note:simple-linear-regression-model) and the [SR Assumptions](note:sr-assumptions), derives the [OLS Estimator](note:ols-estimator), and shows that it is unbiased under linearity, [Strict Exogeneity](note:strict-exogeneity) and variation in $x$, and BLUE once [Homoskedasticity](note:homoskedasticity) and no autocorrelation are added ([Gauss-Markov Theorem](note:gauss-markov-theorem)). The [Sampling Distribution of OLS](note:sampling-distribution-of-ols) then supports inference: [Hypothesis Tests on Regression Coefficients](note:hypothesis-tests-on-regression-coefficients), the [Coefficient of Determination](note:coefficient-of-determination) and [Confidence vs Prediction Intervals](note:confidence-vs-prediction-intervals).

[Econ 430 L4 Cross-Validation and the Bootstrap](note:econ-430-l4-cross-validation-and-the-bootstrap) uses resampling to ask how well a model predicts new data ([Cross-Validation](note:cross-validation)) and how much its estimates would vary ([Bootstrapping OLS](note:bootstrapping-ols)). [Econ 430 L5 Estimating Nonlinear Relationships](note:econ-430-l5-estimating-nonlinear-relationships) fits curves by transforming variables ([Functional Forms and Elasticities](note:functional-forms-and-elasticities), [Box-Cox and Power Transformations](note:box-cox-and-power-transformations)). [Econ 430 L6 Indicator Variables and the OLS Workflow](note:econ-430-l6-indicator-variables-and-the-ols-workflow) adds categorical regressors ([Indicator Variables](note:indicator-variables)) and a seven-step workflow of fitting, testing and [Regression Diagnostics](note:regression-diagnostics). [Econ 430 L7 The Classical Linear Regression Model](note:econ-430-l7-the-classical-linear-regression-model) restates everything in matrix form: [OLS in Matrix Form](note:ols-in-matrix-form), the [Projection Matrix and Residual Maker](note:projection-matrix-and-residual-maker) and the [Conditional Mean vs Linear Projection](note:conditional-mean-vs-linear-projection). The matrix algebra it relies on is in [Math Prep](note:math-prep).

| Block | Lecture | Topics | Weight |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Looking at data | L1, L2 | [EDA for Regression](note:eda-for-regression), [Q-Q Plot](note:q-q-plot), [Skewness and Kurtosis](note:skewness-and-kurtosis), [Lowess Smoother](note:lowess-smoother) | Low to medium |
| Model and OLS | L3 | [SR Assumptions](note:sr-assumptions), [OLS Estimator](note:ols-estimator), [Gauss-Markov Theorem](note:gauss-markov-theorem), [Sampling Distribution of OLS](note:sampling-distribution-of-ols), [Hypothesis Tests on Regression Coefficients](note:hypothesis-tests-on-regression-coefficients), [Coefficient of Determination](note:coefficient-of-determination), [Confidence vs Prediction Intervals](note:confidence-vs-prediction-intervals) | **Highest** |
| Resampling | L4 | [Cross-Validation](note:cross-validation), [Bootstrapping OLS](note:bootstrapping-ols) | Medium |
| Transformations | L5 | [Functional Forms and Elasticities](note:functional-forms-and-elasticities), [Box-Cox and Power Transformations](note:box-cox-and-power-transformations) | **High** |
| Categorical and diagnostics | L6 | [Indicator Variables](note:indicator-variables), [Regression Diagnostics](note:regression-diagnostics) | Medium |
| Matrix theory | L7 | [OLS in Matrix Form](note:ols-in-matrix-form), [Projection Matrix and Residual Maker](note:projection-matrix-and-residual-maker), [Conditional Mean vs Linear Projection](note:conditional-mean-vs-linear-projection), [Full Rank and Identification](note:full-rank-and-identification) | **High** |

The Fall 2025 midterm matches these weights: about half of it is interpretation of log, log-log and quadratic models, Box-Cox output, $t$ tests, $R^2$ and forecast intervals (L3 and L5), with one matrix derivation ($\mathbf{M}\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{0}$, L7), and short answers on bootstrapping, Q-Q plots and normality tests (L1, L4, L6). Its multiple-regression questions (omitted variables, interactions, RESET, Mallows' $C_p$, White's test) go beyond L1 to L7.

sections.heading: If you only have one evening

blocks.md: Derive $\mathbf{b} = (\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{X})^{-1}\mathbf{X}'\mathbf{y}$ from scratch; prove $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{X} = \mathbf{0}$ and $\mathbf{M}\mathbf{M} = \mathbf{M}$; derive the four rows of the functional-form table by differentiating. Those three cover most of what the hard questions can touch.
